chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: The union fines Cab for bringing in a non-union musician
summary: The New York local fined Cab $1,000 for hiring Barefield, until Barefield produced a conditional international card because his Kansas City charter had lapsed.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Now, the union grabbed Cab for bringing me into New York. I wasn't a member of the union. Brought him in. In between theaters and Cotton Club we had to go to the union meetings before the trial board. This went on for a couple of weeks. And he was driving back and forth. And finally they decided to fine Cab $1,000.00 for bringing a non-union musician into New York to work on a steady job.

Now, I hadn't said a word during all these hearings. It was all Cab and them and we're sitting there and I'm just in the middle. So finally after they sentenced him to $1,000.00 fine they said, by the way, what union do you belong to? And I reached in my pocket and pulled out my union card. And at the time I was in Baltimore. Kansas City, which I did belong to, had lost their charter.

Yeah, I had a Kansas City card and they had lost their charter. So in order to work in Baltimore you had to have a card. So we had a card from the international body from Croyningood, which stated this was a conditional card. And it's valid until you find a union where you could join. So they had to take the fine back from Cab and just charged me to join the union.
Why hadn't they asked to see your card to begin with?
You know how they do those things.
Their problem grievance was that any time you bring an out of town -- that's why Welloff (PHONETIC) Cooper lost their charter, by bringing an out of town musician in to a steady job.
At the Regal. So they didn't think about me having a conditional card. All they thought, that I was from out of town. So that's probably why --
Was the six months rule in effect then?
Yes, it was. But I came right into the Cotton Club. So then I played with Cab all that summer, all that winter in the Cotton Club.
